label: Khartoum
sub: Sudan's capital; epicenter of the 2023 war outbreak. RSF seized most of the city within weeks; SAF recaptured it in March 2025 after a major counteroffensive.

label: Omdurman
sub: Twin city to Khartoum across the White Nile; heavily contested throughout the war. SAF recaptured RSF-held western Omdurman in January 2025. On May 13, 2026, SAF cleared Al-Jami'a and Al-Shaqla neighborhoods in southern Omdurman — the last significant RSF pockets in the metro area.

label: Bahri (Khartoum North)
sub: Third city of the Khartoum metro area, site of key oil refinery. SAF retook Bahri in January 2025 after months of intense urban fighting.

label: Khartoum International Airport
sub: Seized by RSF in the opening hours of April 15, 2023; recaptured by SAF in March 2025. Resumed commercial flights for the first time since the war in late April 2026. Targeted by RSF/UAE drone May 4–5, 2026 (intercepted; airport closed 4 days). Reopened May 8–9 after NOTAM issued; Badr Airlines resumed flights May 9, Tarco and Sudanair set to resume May 10. Sudan presented UNSC evidence linking 4 drone attacks since March 1 to UAE-supplied munitions from Bahir Dar, Ethiopia.

label: Presidential Palace
sub: Targeted by RSF on April 15, 2023; became a symbolic battleground. SAF retook the palace complex in March 2025 as a major symbolic victory.

label: Port Sudan
sub: SAF government headquarters; Sudan's primary Red Sea port and de facto wartime capital. Hosts the internationally recognized 'Hope Government' of Gen. Burhan.

label: El Fasher
sub: Capital of North Darfur; last SAF stronghold in Darfur. Fell to RSF in October 2025 after an 18-month siege, triggering mass atrocities described as genocide against Zaghawa and Fur communities.

label: El Geneina
sub: Capital of West Darfur; site of the 2023 Massalit massacres. Between April and November 2023, RSF and allied militias killed an estimated 10,000–15,000 people, primarily Massalit civilians.

label: Nyala
sub: Capital of South Darfur and Sudan's second-largest city. Captured by RSF in October 2023; now hosts the RSF's 'Government of Peace and Unity' alongside Darfur's parallel administration.

label: Wad Madani
sub: Capital of Gezira State; fell to RSF December 19, 2023, displacing 1M+ people. Recaptured by SAF in January 2025 after 13 months of RSF occupation.

label: El Obeid (Al-Ubayyid)
sub: Capital of North Kordofan State; besieged by RSF for nearly two years. SAF broke the siege in February 2025, securing a key central Sudan logistics hub. UN experts warned Aug 7, 2026 of El Fasher-style atrocity risk amid near-constant drone strikes, cholera, and water shortages. An RSF drone strike destroyed the city's main power transformer (reported Aug 20, 2026), knocking out water pumping, hospitals, and phone service citywide; roughly 15,000 families fled into the city over the prior three weeks, part of 200,000+ newly displaced across Kordofan since late 2025 (IOM).

label: Abu Zaima
sub: Town in North Kordofan State. SAF drone struck the local market on May 9, 2026, killing at least 5 civilians.

label: Kassala
sub: Eastern Sudan city; saw clashes on April 15, 2023, but SAF maintained control. Serves as a staging point for refugee movements to Ethiopia and Eritrea.

label: Atbara
sub: River port city in northern Sudan; SAF logistics hub. Remained under SAF control throughout the conflict, serving as a key supply corridor to the front lines.

label: Dongola
sub: Capital of Northern State; remained firmly under SAF control. Key administrative center and rear logistics base for SAF northern operations.

label: Sennar Dam
sub: Critical hydroelectric and irrigation dam on the Blue Nile. Control of Sennar Dam and the surrounding area was contested between SAF and RSF; damage would threaten agricultural irrigation across central Sudan.

label: Merowe
sub: Northern Sudan city near a key dam; RSF deployed forces here before the war, triggering the final confrontation with SAF. SAF retained Merowe throughout the conflict.

label: Zamzam IDP Camp
sub: North Darfur; home to ~500,000 IDPs. First site of declared famine in August 2024. RSF assaulted the camp in April 2025, killing hundreds to over 1,500 civilians.

label: Abu Shouk IDP Camp
sub: El Fasher, North Darfur; major IDP camp adjacent to the city. Came under RSF attack during the El Fasher siege, destroying water facilities and aid supply lines.

label: Tawila
sub: North Darfur town with significant IDP population; contested between SAF garrison and RSF forces during the El Fasher siege. Site of humanitarian access disputes.

label: Nertiti
sub: North Darfur town; fell to RSF control as part of their Darfur-wide campaign. Site of reported RSF looting and civilian displacement.

label: Zalingei
sub: Capital of Central Darfur State; fell to RSF as part of their comprehensive Darfur offensive. SAF forces were expelled or defected; RSF gained full state capital control.

label: Al Daein
sub: Capital of East Darfur State; under RSF control. Site of reported atrocities against non-Arab communities and a major node in RSF's Darfur supply chain.

label: Ardamata Neighborhood
sub: El Geneina neighborhood; site of the November 8, 2023 massacre where RSF and Janjaweed killed 800–2,000 Massalit civilians. One of the worst single atrocities of the war.

label: Jebel Marra
sub: Mountainous Darfur region historically held by Sudan Liberation Army-AW; remained contested with RSF advances. Jebel Marra's population includes many Fur ethnic community members.

label: Gedaref
sub: Eastern Sudan agricultural city; SAF-controlled. Major reception point for IDPs fleeing Khartoum and Gezira. Faces significant strain on infrastructure from displaced population.

label: Sennar
sub: Capital of Sennar State; saw fighting between SAF and RSF as RSF advanced from Gezira. Site of significant IDP flows from Wad Madani's fall.

label: Port Sudan Displacement Sites
sub: Major IDP hub near Port Sudan receiving hundreds of thousands of Khartoum and Darfur refugees. Overwhelmed local resources; multiple informal settlement areas established.

label: Adre Border Crossing
sub: Sudan-Chad border point near El Geneina; only authorized cross-border humanitarian aid entry point into Darfur. SAF and RSF both sought to control access at Adre.

label: Tuine Refugee Camp (Chad)
sub: Chad-side camp receiving Darfur refugees. Over 600,000 Sudanese refugees fled into Chad's eastern regions; border camps became severely overcrowded by mid-2023.

label: Renk (South Sudan Border)
sub: South Sudan border town receiving Sudanese refugees, primarily from Khartoum and Kordofan. UNHCR reported massive influx; Renk became the primary entry point into South Sudan.

label: SAF General Command HQ
sub: Sudanese Armed Forces headquarters in Khartoum; primary military target in the opening hours of April 15, 2023. SAF defended and ultimately retained this complex.

label: Gezira Agricultural Zone
sub: Sudan's breadbasket; RSF seized this region in late 2023, imposing 'taxes' on farmers and looting harvests. RSF control disrupted food production for millions.

label: Jebel Amer Gold Mines
sub: North Darfur gold mining area; controlled by RSF. One of Sudan's richest artisanal gold sites, generating estimated $860M annually for RSF through Al Junaid corporation.

label: Wadi Halfa
sub: Far northern Sudan near Egyptian border; remained under SAF control. Entry point for refugees crossing into Egypt; Egyptian forces maintained presence in the area.

label: Kadugli
sub: Capital of South Kordofan State; IPC Phase 5 famine confirmed (WFP/FAO/UNICEF May 2026). Road blockaded by RSF-SPLM-N siege since January 2026. SAF broke the Dilling siege for a third time on May 20, 2026 and the first supply convoy since January arrived the same day — 12 trucks of food and medicine; sugar prices collapsed from SDG 40,000 to SDG 13,000/kg. Civilians celebrated in the streets.

label: Dilling
sub: Second-largest city in South Kordofan; besieged three times in 2026 by RSF-SPLM-N forces. SAF broke the siege for a third time on May 19–20, 2026, recapturing Al-Takma (~7 km east) and reopening the Dilling–Kadugli road; a supply convoy reached famine-confirmed Kadugli the same day. Sudan Doctors Network warned of El Fasher-scale catastrophe earlier in the siege cycle.

label: Khartoum Oil Refinery (Bahri)
sub: Major oil refinery north of Khartoum; retaken by SAF in January 2025. Its recapture restored critical fuel production capacity and was a key strategic objective of the SAF counteroffensive.

label: El Obeid Airport
sub: North Kordofan airport used by SAF as a logistics hub. Remained a key SAF resupply point during the siege of El Obeid city; RSF failed to capture the airfield.

label: Mellit
sub: North Darfur town; fell to RSF during their encirclement of El Fasher. Blocking of Mellit road cut off a key resupply route to the besieged El Fasher garrison.

label: Edd Port
sub: Red Sea port used by SAF for supplies. Secondary logistics entry point alongside Port Sudan for SAF resupply from regional allies including Egypt and Turkey.

label: Damazin
sub: Capital of Blue Nile State near the Roseires Dam. SAF-held strategic city near Ethiopia border. Site of cross-border aid routes for some Sudanese refugees.

label: Halayib Triangle
sub: Disputed territory claimed by both Sudan and Egypt; Egyptian forces present. Egypt's support for the SAF made this border region strategically significant for SAF logistics.

label: El Fasher Teaching Hospital
sub: Only major functioning hospital in North Darfur during the El Fasher siege. Under repeated threat of RSF attacks; WHO documented attempts to attack the medical facility.

label: Gezira IDP Sites
sub: Multiple IDP settlement areas across Gezira State following RSF takeover of December 2023. Over 1 million people displaced; many sought shelter in SAF-held areas to the east.

label: South Khartoum
sub: Southern districts of Khartoum including Jabal Awliya; saw protracted fighting between SAF and RSF. Significant civilian displacement and infrastructure destruction throughout 2023–2024.

label: Halfa El Jadida
sub: Town in River Nile State; remained SAF-controlled throughout the conflict. Part of the northern Sudan corridor connecting Port Sudan to central SAF forces.

label: Kassala Refugee & IDP Zone
sub: Kassala State hosts hundreds of thousands of Sudanese IDPs from Khartoum and Blue Nile, as well as Eritrean refugees. Healthcare and food security severely strained.

label: Tine Border Crossing
sub: South Darfur border crossing to Chad; key route for Sudanese refugees and limited humanitarian aid. Control contested and access restricted by both SAF and RSF at various times.

label: Shendi
sub: River Nile State town; SAF-held logistics and resupply point between Port Sudan and the Khartoum front. Used as a staging area for SAF forces during the capital counteroffensive.

label: Abu Hamad
sub: River Nile State junction town; SAF controlled. Key road and rail junction on the Nile for moving supplies south toward Khartoum.

label: En Nahud
sub: West Kordofan town; came under RSF influence as the conflict expanded from Darfur into Kordofan. RSF used as a supply route connecting Darfur to central Sudan.

label: Bahri Displacement Zone
sub: Khartoum North IDP concentration area; hundreds of thousands fled fighting in Bahri, one of the war's most active urban battle zones through late 2024.

label: Geneina Airport
sub: El Geneina International Airport; site of the June 14, 2023 assassination of West Darfur Governor Khamis Abakar. RSF controlled the airport throughout the West Darfur campaign.

label: South Kordofan Battle Zone
sub: Broad area of South Kordofan contested between SAF and RSF forces as of 2025–2026. SAF pushing westward from reclaimed Khartoum; RSF defending Kordofan corridor linking Darfur.

label: Omdurman Hospital District
sub: Omdurman's hospital district severely impacted by fighting. Multiple facilities damaged or occupied by fighters. MSF and ICRC reported inability to access and operate safely.

label: Nyala Airport
sub: South Darfur's main airport; captured by RSF in October 2023 with the fall of Nyala. Became an RSF logistics hub for supplying Darfur operations.

label: Wadi Salih (Mukjar area)
sub: Central Darfur locality with significant non-Arab population; heavily affected by RSF atrocities and displacement. Entire communities of Fur and Masalit fled the area in 2023.

label: Kassab IDP Camp
sub: North Darfur IDP camp north of El Fasher; received massive influx during the El Fasher siege. RSF attacks on surrounding areas threatened camp access roads.

label: Jabal Awliya Dam IDP Zone
sub: South Khartoum area near Jabal Awliya Dam; became an IDP gathering point as civilians fled fighting in the capital. Overcrowded with limited food and water access.

label: Roseires Dam
sub: Blue Nile State hydroelectric dam; SAF-controlled strategic infrastructure. One of Sudan's key power generators; RSF attacks on power infrastructure threatened dam operations.

label: Abu Zabad
sub: West Kordofan town; RSF seized as part of corridor between Darfur and central Sudan. SAF airstrikes targeted RSF positions in the area.

label: Bara
sub: North Kordofan town, second-largest in the state, ~45km east of El Obeid. RSF held it from March 16, 2026 until SAF and allied forces recaptured Bara alongside Al-Baraka and Um Sayala on July 25, 2026, destroying 73 RSF vehicles and easing pressure on besieged El Obeid. RSF has since targeted the town with repeated long-range drone strikes, including two FH-95 drones downed by SAF air defenses on Aug 17, 2026.

label: Kurmuk
sub: Blue Nile State town on the Ethiopia border; captured by RSF-SPLM-N alliance on March 23, 2026. About 73,000 people fled; the fall threatens Ed Damazin and the Roseires Dam. Sudan accused Ethiopia of facilitating the assault.

label: Sarf Umra
sub: North Darfur town under RSF control; struck by SAF drones on March 26, 2026 hitting the main market, government HQ, and a fuel tanker with civilian casualties reported.

label: Ad Dabbah
sub: Northern State town on the Nile; struck by RSF drone on March 21, 2026 killing 6 people and damaging the engineering college and electricity substation. Demonstrated RSF's long-range drone reach into deep SAF-controlled territory. Site of a 318-strong RSF defection to SAF on August 19, 2026 — including 4 commanders and up to 50 combat vehicles — part of an accelerating wave of RSF defections.

label: Lagawa
sub: West Kordofan town under RSF control; struck twice by SAF drones in March 2026 — March 23 (15 killed) and March 27 (15 killed) — killing 30+ in residential neighborhoods.

label: Ed Damazin
sub: Capital of Blue Nile State near the Roseires Dam; SAF-held but threatened by RSF-SPLM-N advance after fall of Kurmuk on March 23, 2026. Loss would cut power to central and eastern Sudan.

label: Al Sunut
sub: West Kordofan town under RSF control; struck by SAF drones twice in March 2026 — March 10 (50+ killed in lorry strike) and March 27 (7 killed at funeral, 39 wounded). Pattern of repeated drone targeting.

label: Geissan
sub: Blue Nile district ~200 km southeast of Ed Damazin; RSF-SPLM-N military buildup on March 28, 2026 forced 425+ families to flee. Its fall would directly threaten Ed Damazin and the Roseires Dam.

label: Al-Rahad
sub: North Kordofan town; hit by SAF drone strike on March 26, 2026 targeting a civilian passenger vehicle, killing 6 and injuring 12. Part of the wave of attacks across Kordofan and Darfur.

label: Dalang
sub: Nuba Mountains city in South Kordofan; site of a major RSF multi-front assault on April 2, 2026 that was repelled by SAF forces. RSF assault cohesion weakened by tribal tensions within recruited units.

label: Al-Jabalain
sub: White Nile State town; RSF drone strikes on April 3, 2026 struck Al-Jabalain Hospital's operating theater and maternity ward during an immunization campaign, killing 10 (including 7 medical staff) and wounding 19. Attack in SAF-controlled territory confirmed RSF long-range drone reach.

label: Rabak
sub: Capital of White Nile State; RSF drone struck a medical supply depot in Rabak on April 3-4, 2026, concurrent with the Al-Jabalain Hospital attack, further degrading healthcare capacity in SAF-controlled White Nile State.

label: Wadi al-Hout
sub: North Kordofan area; SAF repelled a large-scale RSF ground assault on April 6, 2026, preventing RSF from reversing SAF territorial gains in North Kordofan made since the relief of El Obeid and recapture of Bara.

label: Al-Tukma
sub: Strategic area ~7km east of Dilling, South Kordofan; SAF forces seized Al-Tukma from RSF-SPLM-N on April 8, 2026, reopening the Dilling–North Kordofan road and breaking the RSF partial siege of Dilling.

label: Damrat al-Firdous
sub: Central Darfur area under RSF control; site of a SAF drone strike on April 8, 2026 that killed Hamid Ali Abubakar, commander-in-chief of the RSF-aligned Sudanese Awakening Revolutionary Council (RAC) and security adviser to Hemedti, during a command meeting.

label: Umm Dukhun
sub: Central Darfur district under RSF control; struck by drone fire on April 16, 2026 — at least 8 munitions fired, killing 24+ civilians and injuring approximately 20 others.

label: El Fula (Al-Fula)
sub: Capital of West Kordofan State; drone strike hit El Wahda market on April 16, 2026, killing 9 civilians (3 women, 6 children).

label: Kutum
sub: North Darfur town ~100 km northwest of El Fasher; under RSF control. Site of a drone strike on April 10, 2026 that struck a wedding gathering in the Al-Salama neighborhood, killing at least 30 including 17 children and injuring 107. UN Secretary-General condemned the attack.

label: Muqja Station
sub: Blue Nile State railway station between Kurmuk and Ed Damazin. Captured by RSF-SPLM-N after the fall of Kurmuk (March 23, 2026); recaptured by SAF's 4th Infantry Division on April 21, 2026. Controls the supply axis to the Roseires Dam.

label: Sultan Medical Complex (El Geneina)
sub: Medical facility in RSF-controlled El Geneina, West Darfur. Struck by a drone on April 20, 2026, killing 3 people and igniting fires — the latest in a pattern of healthcare attacks across Sudan with 2,052+ killed in 217+ attacks documented by WHO.

label: Um Dukhun
sub: Town in Central Darfur's Buram locality near the Chad border. Struck by SAF drones on April 17, 2026, killing 24+ civilians in market areas including an entire family of six; part of a combined 44-civilian death toll across Darfur and North Kordofan in that single day.

label: Al-Hamidiyah IDP Camp
sub: Displaced persons camp on the outskirts of RSF-controlled Zalingei, Central Darfur. SAF drone strike at dawn on April 27, 2026 killed 6 civilians and injured 15, destroying multiple homes. The camp shelters thousands of displaced women and children who fled fighting across Darfur. Documented by Emergency Lawyers Sudan.

label: Kosti
sub: Major White Nile State city ~320 km south of Khartoum; SAF 18th Infantry Division headquarters. Struck by RSF drone wave on April 29, 2026 alongside Kenana airbase in a coordinated attack on SAF military installations.

label: Kenana Airbase
sub: SAF aviation and logistics installation in White Nile State near Kenana Sugar Company. Struck by RSF drones on April 29, 2026 as part of a coordinated wave targeting SAF military positions south of Khartoum.

label: Labado
sub: East Darfur displacement area under RSF control. Site of a measles outbreak documented in April 2026 that has killed ~70 people and infected ~1,000 since March, reflecting collapsed healthcare infrastructure in RSF-controlled Darfur.

label: Singa (Sennar Capital)
sub: Capital of Sennar State on the Blue Nile, ~300 km southeast of Khartoum. Site of April 30, 2026 RSF drone strike on an SAF military base during a high-level meeting of commanders and officials — 27 killed, 73 wounded, senior officers among the dead. Sennar State Governor survived.

label: Al-Kahli Zaidan
sub: Village in Al Jazirah (Gezira) State, ~40 km east of Wad Madani. Site of an RSF targeted drone strike on May 2, 2026 that killed 9–17 family members of Sudan Shield Forces commander Abu Aqla Kaikal — including his brothers, fellow SSF commanders, and six children. Gen. Burhan visited the site to condole. RSF targeted Kaikal for defecting from the RSF in October 2024 and helping SAF recapture Al Jazirah.

label: Gedaref
sub: Capital of Gedaref State in eastern Sudan; SAF-controlled major city on the Ethiopian border corridor. As of May 2026, Sudan reinforced forces in Gedaref State (East Gallabat, Basunda, Al-Fashaga) in response to accusations that Ethiopia permitted RSF drone launches from Bahir Dar Airport. Key logistics hub for SAF eastern operations.

label: East Gallabat
sub: Sudan-Ethiopia border crossing point in Gedaref State. Site of SAF border reinforcement in May 2026 after Sudan accused Ethiopia of facilitating RSF drone attacks launched from Bahir Dar Airport. Sudan deployed additional ground forces and anti-aircraft systems here as diplomatic confrontation with Addis Ababa escalated.

label: Al Quz
sub: Town in South Kordofan State; struck by RSF drone on May 8, 2026, killing civilians. Part of the SAF-RSF contested zone in South Kordofan where SAF is pushing counteroffensive operations against RSF-SPLM-N forces. Documented in OHCHR's May 11 high-alert statement.

label: RSF Forces at Libya-Egypt-Sudan Border
sub: Far northwest Sudan, where Sudan, Libya, and Egypt converge near the Libyan Desert (Jebel Uweinat area). RSF forces reportedly massing here as of May 2026 (MadaMasr), potentially establishing a new supply corridor through Libyan territory via RSF-LNA networks. Unconfirmed by independent sources.

label: Al-Hamadi
sub: Administrative hub for the Hawazma tribe in central South Kordofan. Retaken by SAF ground forces on May 13, 2026, as part of SAF's sustained westward push through South Kordofan against the RSF-held Darfur–Kordofan corridor.

label: Al Zorg
sub: North Darfur village; ancestral hometown and tribal heartland of RSF commander Hemedti (Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo). SAF airstrikes in May 2026 killed at least 64 civilians, destroyed the local hospital, and killed two of Hemedti's relatives and tribal leader Bashir Barma Baraka Allah — one of the war's highest-profile SAF strikes on a location tied to RSF leadership.

label: Khor Hassan
sub: Strategic town in southeastern Blue Nile State on the Kurmuk–Ed Damazin axis. RSF-SPLM-N controlled the area following the March 23, 2026 Kurmuk offensive; recaptured by SAF's 4th Infantry Division on May 16, 2026 as part of the methodical SAF rollback of RSF-SPLM-N Blue Nile gains.

label: Wadi al-Atrun
sub: Remote desert town in Al-Malha locality, far northern North Darfur. Captured by SAF on May 19, 2026, severing an RSF trans-Saharan supply corridor from the Libyan Desert (Kufra) southward into Darfur — used by RSF and Libya-based allies (Haftar LNA networks) for weapons, fuel, and fighter resupply. Part of SAF's multi-axis supply interdiction campaign alongside Gedaref border reinforcement and the Nyala aerial campaign.

label: Ghubaysh
sub: Town in West Kordofan State under RSF control. Site of a drone strike on May 19, 2026 that killed at least 28 people in a crowded market — witnesses described a two-stage attack hitting an RSF vehicle then a packed restaurant. One of the deadliest single drone strikes of May 2026. SAF denied responsibility.

label: Dilling Medical Warehouses
sub: City medical supply warehouses in Dilling, South Kordofan. Completely destroyed by an RSF/SPLM-N drone strike on May 20–21, 2026 — injuring 6 and depriving thousands of patients of medicines. The attack came within 24–48 hours of SAF breaking the Dilling siege for the third time and reopening the Kadugli road.

label: Dibebad (Ed Dubeibat)
sub: Strategic crossroads in the 'Tayba Triangle' of South Kordofan, linking northern, western, and southern Kordofan routes. Captured by SAF on May 23, 2026; IOM documented 565 households displaced in the fighting. The capture tightens SAF's cordon on RSF-SPLM-N logistics between Dilling, Kadugli, and Buram.

label: Yabus Area (Blue Nile)
sub: Border area in Blue Nile State near the Ethiopia-Sudan frontier, in the RSF-SPLM-N-controlled zone following the fall of Kurmuk (March 23, 2026). Site of a SAF airstrike on May 23, 2026 that struck an RSF-SPLM-N supply convoy — killing 5 and injuring 20. Part of SAF's sustained aerial interdiction of the Kurmuk–Ed Damazin RSF-SPLM-N logistics axis.

label: Al-Tina (Chad Border)
sub: West Darfur border town on the Sudan-Chad frontier in the Adre-Tine crossing area — the primary refugee and humanitarian aid corridor into Darfur. On May 25, 2026, an RSF drone struck the weekly market, killing at least 14 civilians (mostly women vendors). Chad condemned the attack as aggression against its territorial integrity, closed the Sudan border, and convened an emergency Defence & Security Council. The border closure threatens the main conduit for millions of Sudanese refugees and WFP/UNHCR humanitarian operations in Darfur.

label: Mustariha (RAC Headquarters)
sub: North Darfur town and base of operations for the Sudanese Awakening Revolutionary Council (RAC) led by Sheikh Musa Hilal. On May 25, 2026, RSF drones struck Hilal's guesthouse compound in an apparent assassination attempt — Hilal survived, his son was injured, and several RAC commanders were killed. The RAC is a SAF-aligned Rizeigat Arab faction that split from Hemedti before the 2023 war.

label: Misterei
sub: Predominantly Masalit town in northern West Darfur. On May 28, 2026, RSF fighters and allied Arab militias launched a coordinated ground assault, killing 28–97 civilians with assault rifles, RPGs, and vehicle-mounted weapons. Satellite fire detection confirmed active fires May 29–June 2; imagery showed extensive burn marks across all residential areas. One of at least seven West Darfur towns burned by RSF since April 2026.

label: Al-Murrah Area
sub: Rural area west of Barah town, North Kordofan State. On May 29, 2026 — the second day of Eid al-Adha — an RSF convoy of ~20 combat vehicles attacked villages al-Murrah, Umm Sadoun al-Sharif, and al-Radah, killing 60 civilians (confirmed June 2 by Sudan Tribune/Doctors Network). No military presence in the targeted villages. Sudan's Foreign Ministry formally condemned the massacre on June 2 and called on the UNSC to act.

label: Kabum
sub: Town in western South Darfur, ~120 km west of Nyala. On June 1, 2026, a drone struck a gathering of civilians and military personnel near Kabum, killing at least 12 people and critically injuring several others. The drone approached from the east and fired 3 missiles in two passes. TASIS (Sudan Founding Alliance) accused the SAF; attribution is disputed. The area also saw concurrent Salamat-Beni Halba tribal clashes using RSF-supplied weapons.

label: Qaysan District
sub: Administrative district in southern Blue Nile State. SAF retook five towns here on May 26, 2026 (Abdaqla, Adi, Washimbu, Um Shanqar, Kinshinkaru), forcing RSF and SPLM-N (al-Hilu) forces to retreat toward the Ethiopian border. Part of SAF's accelerating Blue Nile counteroffensive following the RSF-SPLM-N capture of Kurmuk (March 23, 2026).

label: Abu Zabad
sub: Town in West Kordofan State on the road to state capital Al-Fula. RSF drone struck civilian vehicles on the Abu Zabad–Al-Fula road on May 30, 2026, killing 10 people. West Kordofan has seen approximately 46,000 new displacements during May 2026 due to escalating RSF drone attacks and ground combat.

label: Al-Baraka
sub: Garrison town in southern Blue Nile State, on the Kurmuk–Ed Damazin strategic corridor. Scene of intense SAF vs. RSF-SPLM-N fighting on June 3–4, 2026, with both sides claiming control. SAF's 4th Infantry Division reported repelling the attack. The town's fall would threaten the Roseires Dam and Ed Damazin city.

label: Abu Jubeiha
sub: Town in the Rashad locality of the Nuba Mountains, South Kordofan State. SAF-held strategic outpost in an active combat zone where SAF faces RSF-SPLM-N (al-Hilu) pressure. Targeted by RSF drones in the coordinated multi-state dawn campaign on June 5, 2026, alongside simultaneous strikes on Omdurman and Ed Damazin.

label: Kulbus
sub: Strategic town on the Chad border in West Darfur, between army-held Al-Tina and RSF-held El Geneina. SAF-allied Joint Forces claimed capture on June 30, 2026 — the army's largest western Darfur gain since losing El Fasher in Oct 2025 — but RSF regained the town on July 10, 2026 after reinforcing with armor from El Geneina, Saraf Omra, and Kabkabiya.

label: Al-Sayyah
sub: Major weekly trading hub in North Darfur serving Al-Malha, Al-Kuma, and Malit. A drone strike alleged to be SAF hit the town's main market on June 22, 2026, killing one and destroying an estimated 100 million SDG in goods.

label: Jabal al-Uqaydat
sub: Artisanal gold-mining site in River Nile State near the disputed Halayeb Triangle and Egyptian border. Struck by fixed-wing aircraft and drones on June 16, 2026, killing 15-30 (contested), in an operation Egyptian sources said targeted informal mining/smuggling networks tied to RSF gold-financing routes. Attribution to Egypt unconfirmed by Cairo.

label: Ambara-Tine Corridor Villages
sub: Cluster of Zaghawa-inhabited villages (Qarboura, Oruwa, Um Marahik, Kourbia, Abu Leiha, Ana Baji) along the Ambara-Tine road near the Chad border, North Darfur. Razed by a large RSF force beginning July 1, 2026; homes and markets burned, wells destroyed, livestock looted. 3,500+ displaced from Wadi Fungo village alone by July 3.

label: Kauda
sub: Main stronghold of Abdel Aziz al-Hilu's SPLM-N faction in the Nuba Mountains, South Kordofan. Seized by a rival Otoro-ethnicity faction on June 22, 2026 following a tribal border dispute, expelling SPLM-N administration and marking a significant internal fracture in the RSF's Kordofan-front SPLM-N alliance.

label: Al-Bar
sub: SPLM-N (Toka faction) outpost in Geissan district, Blue Nile State, near the Ethiopian border. Captured by SAF's 13th Infantry Brigade on June 23, 2026 as part of a broader offensive that culminated in the recapture of Kurmuk on July 8.

label: Ambro / Furuawiya
sub: North Darfur villages near the Chad border captured by RSF forces June 23-24, 2026 as part of a renewed Chad-border offensive; 2,200+ displaced from the nearby Orshi Reservoir area in the preceding week.

label: Bir Saliba
sub: Strategic area ~30km north of El Geneina, West Darfur — the RSF's last major stronghold in the region. Joint Force fighters allied with SAF repelled RSF assaults here on August 4 (killing RSF commander Mahdi Adam, 'Jebel Moon') and again on August 8, 2026, when the RSF attempted an encirclement from multiple directions.

label: Sirba Region
sub: West Darfur region near El Geneina where renewed RSF offensive activity displaced more than 6,650 people from 11 villages by Aug 8, 2026; UN OCHA reported the toll had grown to roughly 18,000 people displaced from 20+ villages over the week to Aug 10, 2026, most fleeing across the border into Chad.

label: El Obeid — Atrocity Risk Warning
sub: UN experts warned August 7, 2026 of an El Fasher-style mass atrocity risk in besieged El Obeid, where hundreds of thousands face near-constant drone strikes (as many as 40 at once), a worsening cholera outbreak, critical water shortages, and reported sexual violence. North Kordofan recorded the highest number of drone attacks in Sudan in 2026. UN OCHA said Aug 10 the RSF had encircled the city, with drone attacks continuing even as civilians flee there for safety; humanitarian partners delivered 2 million liters of drinking water to roughly 133,000 residents. RSF ground assaults on approach routes (Umm Arada, Jabal al-Hashaba) intensified Aug 14.

label: Kurmuk
sub: Blue Nile State town near the Ethiopian border. A mass grave with 25 civilians executed by the RSF was discovered here Aug 9, 2026, more than a month after SAF recaptured the town (Jul 8). The RSF recaptured Kurmuk on Aug 13, 2026 as SAF withdrew — the second Blue Nile town it seized in a week after Geisan.

label: Geisan
sub: Blue Nile State town near the Ethiopian border. RSF and SPLM-N (al-Hilu) fighters seized large parts of the town on Aug 11, 2026, staging from Ethiopian territory; SAF retained its 13th Infantry Brigade headquarters. UN OCHA reported 20+ civilians killed and ~2,500 displaced.

label: Jabrat al-Shaikh
sub: North Kordofan transport hub. SAF and allied Joint Forces repelled a 250-vehicle RSF assault here on Aug 13, 2026 after nearly two days of RSF troop buildups from Darfur, destroying/capturing dozens of vehicles. Also the site of a separate Aug 12 incident in which Emergency Lawyers accused SAF of killing 5 civilians in the surrounding area.

label: Kauda
sub: South Kordofan (Nuba Mountains) town where SPLM-N (al-Hilu faction) detained ten aid workers in early August 2026 (4 on Aug 6, 6 more on Aug 8) amid clashes with the Otoro tribe, drawing calls for their release from local tribal leadership.

label: Umm Arada
sub: Village roughly 15km southwest of El Obeid, North Kordofan. RSF launched a dawn ground assault here and on the nearby Jabal al-Hashaba hills on Aug 14, 2026, killing 14+ civilians per Emergency Lawyers; RSF claims full control, SAF says it repelled the attack. Site of intensifying fighting over routes into besieged El Obeid.

label: Qardud / Abu Hamama (Otoro Villages)
sub: Otoro-inhabited villages near Kauda in South Kordofan's Nuba Mountains. Sudan Doctors Network reported on August 25, 2026 that SPLM-N (al-Hilu) fighters killed 27 people, including 4 children, in ethnically targeted attacks here, triggering fresh displacement toward Abu Hitan and Kadugli. Extends an ethnic standoff between SPLM-N-aligned forces and the Otoro minority rooted in earlier 2026 land disputes.

label: Mourdi Depression (Chad)
sub: Remote desert depression in Chad's Ennedi-Est province, over 100km from the Sudan border. Chad accused the Sudanese army of striking an RSF-linked resupply convoy here on the evening of August 20, 2026, raising fears of the war spilling into Chad. Chad raised its border alert level; the African Union and US envoy Massad Boulos called for restraint on August 27. Sudan has not acknowledged responsibility.
